blocks.passage:
A working day has many tasks. Some are urgent, some are important, some are small. Good time management is about choosing the right task at the right moment.

Many people start the day with the hardest task, when the mind is fresh. They leave emails for later. They put meetings together, so the rest of the day is for real work.

A calendar is your best friend at work. It helps you see the day, protect time for important things, and say "Sorry, I am busy" when needed.

items.q: What is good time management about?
options: Choosing the right task at the right moment
items.why: "Good time management is about choosing the right task at the right moment."

items.q: When do many people do the hardest task?
options: At the start, when the mind is fresh
At the end of the day
items.why: "Many people start the day with the hardest task, when the mind is fresh."

items.q: What do they do with emails?
items.why: "They leave emails for later."

items.q: Why do they put meetings together?
options: So the rest of the day is for real work
items.why: "They put meetings together, so the rest of the day is for real work."

items.q: What does the text call 'your best friend at work'?
items.why: "A calendar is your best friend at work."

audio.text:
Every morning, before I open my email, I do one small thing that changes my whole day. I write my three top priorities on a sticky note. Let me show you why.

If I open my email first, I lose control immediately. Other people's questions become my whole day, and my own important work never gets done.

So instead, first thing, I ask: what are the three most important things I must do today? Today it's: finish the client report, call the São Paulo supplier, and prepare for the Friday meeting. Three things. I write them on the note.

Then I do the hardest one first — the report — while my mind is fresh. I don't check email until that's done.

After that, I open my email and deal with the rest. Meetings I put together in the afternoon, so my morning stays clear for real work.

Three priorities, hardest first, email later. It sounds small, but at the end of the day, the important things are done — not just the urgent ones.

items.q: What does Emily do every morning before email?
options: Write her three top priorities on a sticky note
items.why: "I write my three top priorities on a sticky note."

items.q: What happens if she opens email first?
options: She loses control — others' questions become her whole day
items.why: "If I open my email first, I lose control immediately."

items.q: What are her three priorities today?
options: Finish the report, call the supplier, prepare for Friday
items.why: "finish the client report, call the São Paulo supplier, and prepare for the Friday meeting."

items.q: Which task does she do first, and why?
options: The hardest one, while her mind is fresh
items.why: "I do the hardest one first — the report — while my mind is fresh."

items.q: When does she schedule meetings?
options: In the afternoon, to keep the morning clear
items.why: "Meetings I put together in the afternoon, so my morning stays clear."

items.q: A **priority** is…
options: a task that matters most and comes first
items.why: Priority = prioridade.

items.q: Something **urgent** is…
options: needs to be done very soon
items.why: Urgent = urgente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **___** helps you see and plan your day."
items.why: Calendar = agenda/calendário.

items.q: **Focus** means…
options: giving your full attention to one thing
items.why: Focus = foco.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I'm very **___** today — three big tasks."
items.why: Busy = ocupado.

items.q: "Do the hardest task **first thing**." First thing means…
options: at the very start of the day
items.why: First thing = logo cedo.

items.q: "Let's **deal with** the emails later." To deal with means to…
items.why: Deal with = lidar com.

items.q: "I need to **protect my time** in the morning." To protect your time means to…
options: keep it free for important work
items.why: Protect your time = proteger seu tempo.

items.q: "Meetings, I **put together** in the afternoon." To put together (meetings) means to…
items.why: Put together = agrupar.

items.q: "Sorry, I'm **tied up** right now." To be tied up means to…
items.why: Tied up = ocupado, sem tempo.
